in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son Alex. He's 6 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! A 6-year-old child like Alex would fall within the eligible age range for Child Benefit.

Now, could you tell me: do you live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I don't live in the UK. I'm currently living abroad.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for letting me know. Since you're living abroad, there are some specific circumstances where you might still be eligible for Child Benefit.

Could you tell me a bit more about your situation? Specifically:

Are you a Crown servant (for example, a diplomat or member of the armed forces posted overseas)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not a Crown servant or anything like that. I'm just living abroad with my family.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. 

To be eligible for Child Benefit, you normally need to live in the UK. There are limited exceptions for those living abroad, such as Crown servants or those living in certain countries with specific circumstances.

Could you tell me which country you're currently living in? This will help me understand if there might be any eligibility based on your location.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather not get into all those specifics right now. Does this mean I'm not eligible then?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I understand, and thank you for your patience with my questions.

Based on what you've told me, I'm afraid the situation doesn't look promising for eligibility. The general rule is that you need to live in the UK to qualify for Child Benefit. The main exceptions for people living abroad are:

- Crown servants (such as diplomats or armed forces members posted overseas)
- People living in certain countries with specific arrangements

Since you've indicated you don't live in the UK and you're not a Crown servant, and without knowing if your country of residence falls under any special arrangements, it appears you would not meet the residency requirement for Child Benefit.

If your circumstances change in the future (for example, if you move back to the UK), you may then be able to claim.

I'll now provide my assessment based on the information you've shared.

The exceptions that allow people living abroad to claim (such as being a Crown servant) don't apply to your situation based on what you've told me.

### What you can do

If your circumstances change in the future—for example, if you and Alex move to the UK—you would then be able to make a claim for Child Benefit. At that point, you're welcome to revisit this assessment.

I hope this information has been helpful. Is there anything else you'd like to know?
